summary: 58-year-old postmenopausal woman: hard irregular lump with skin tethering, nipple retraction and an axillary node. Urgent triple assessment: bilateral mammography, ultrasound (breast and axilla), core biopsy; suspected cancer pathway.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Hard lump in the right breast
inputs.hpi: Hard lump in the right breast for 2 months, getting bigger. Skin over it looks puckered when she lifts her arm. Nipple has started to pull in. Postmenopausal, took HRT for 6 years. No discharge.

exam.other: Breasts: 3 cm hard, irregular mass at 10 o'clock right breast, tethered to skin with dimpling on arm elevation; recent nipple retraction. 1.5 cm firm mobile right axillary node. Left breast normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspicious right breast mass with skin tethering and axillary node — probable carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspicious breast mass (right), 3 cm, skin tethering, nipple retraction and palpable axillary node in a 58-year-old — probable carcinoma. Urgent triple assessment: bilateral mammography, ultrasound breast and axilla, core biopsy (+ axillary node sampling).

mustRankTopK.note: Hard, fixed, tethered lump with nipple retraction and a node.

redFlags.knownGapNote: Triggered but labelled colorectal. cancer-screening.ts labels every triggered screen "colorectal": the colorectal block tests `c.met && c.rule.includes('colorectal') || c.rule.includes('bowel') || …` (operator precedence), which is true whenever any colorectal rule exists, and the breast block keeps the first label (cancerType ?? "breast").
redFlags.proposedFix: Parenthesise the colorectal condition (c.met && (… || … )) in screenForCancer, and assign cancerType per met rule; add a vitest vector for a breast-lump-only screen.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: The pre-histology code N63.0 (breast lump) maps to no management protocol, so the plan is empty. Harness limitation as well: web-runner.ts passes examBreast: "" (the vignette schema has no breast exam field), so the dashboard prompt "Breast Mass → Triple Assessment" (USS, mammogram ≥35, core biopsy) is not exercised.

mustExclude.note: Definitive surgery is planned after histology and MDT, not at the first visit.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

guideline.name: NCCN Guidelines — Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
guideline.section: Palpable mass: age <30 ultrasound first; age ≥30 diagnostic mammography + ultrasound; tissue sampling of suspicious findings; nipple discharge (spontaneous, unilateral, single duct, bloody); skin changes
guideline.citation: National Comprehensive Cancer Network. NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis (current version at authoring).

rationale: Permutation: age 58 and suspicious features. The three imaging/biopsy arms are critical because omitting any of them from triple assessment can miss or understage a cancer.

authoring.author: Claude (hernia / breast / endocrine cluster)
